neighbours.label: the negation "n't" in a first-person statement of incomprehension, where 'understand' / 'get it' is about to follow ("I just don't…")
fire: Everyone keeps laughing at that joke, and I just don't get what is so funny.
People pay thousands for those sneakers, and honestly I just don't see the appeal.
He reread the contract three times and said, "I just don't understand this clause."
They adore that show, but I just don't get why anyone would watch it.
Her teacher explained fractions again, and she sighed, "I just don't get it."
You had a perfect job and you quit, and I just can't understand your reasons.
Fans queue all night for that band, and I just don't see why they bother.
My sister loves horror films, but I just don't get the attraction at all.
quiet: Everyone keeps asking about the schedule, and we don't have the dates yet.
People pay thousands for those sneakers, but the shop doesn't accept returns.
He reread the contract three times and said he wouldn't sign it today.
They adore that show, but the network won't renew it next year.
Her teacher explained fractions again, since the class hadn't finished the chapter.
You had a perfect job and you quit, so you aren't getting a bonus.
Fans queue all night for that band, though the doors don't open until noon.
My sister loves horror films, but our parents didn't let her watch them.

notes: Output direction promotes ' understand', ' understanding', ' understood'. Probes: 'I just don't see why' 0.61, 'I just don't get it' 0.62; 'We don't know yet' 0.01, 'I don't have any money' 0.04, bare ' understand' after 'never' 0.08. The − pole's top examples are "don't" before 'know', the other side of the same distinction.
